findings.title: Alpha Omega's broader composite is classified as exact three-point MACE

evidence.quote: The primary end point was the rate of major cardiovascular events, which comprised fatal and nonfatal cardiovascular events and cardiac interventions.

Neither EPA-DHA nor ALA reduced this primary end point (hazard ratio with EPA-DHA, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.87 to 1.17; P=0.93; hazard ratio with ALA, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.05; P=0.20).

findings.why_wrong: For PMID 20929341, the held definition explicitly includes cardiac interventions. The classifier nevertheless invents an exact cardiovascular-death/MI/stroke component set and reports no extra components. The separate heterogeneity disclosure does not make that classification correct.
findings.served_effect: The HR 1.01 enters the five-study efficacy synthesis with a false exact-target classification and contaminates the canonical endpoint component summary.
findings.proposed_fixture: Use PMID 20929341's held abstract, configured primary outcome, and served source string as inputs to target_endpoint.classify_bound. Assert that cardiac interventions prevent EXACT_TARGET and that the result is not assigned only the three canonical components. Current code returns EXACT_TARGET with no extras.

findings.title: GISSI-HF AF counts are incorrectly declared absent

evidence.quote: Among the 5835 patients without AF at study entry, 444 randomized to n-3 PUFAs (15.2%) and 408 to placebo (14.0%) developed AF (unadjusted hazard 1.10, P = 0.19).

findings.why_wrong: The held abstract reports both arm event counts and percentages. Whether this post-hoc population supplies an admissible pooled estimate is a separate decision from whether numerical AF results are held.
findings.served_effect: The harm audit labels available AF results absent and validates the absence reason as REASON_TRUE.
findings.proposed_fixture: Pass the held PMID 23839902 abstract and configured AF keywords to reason_audit.find_value_in_sources. Assert a non-null result identifying the 444-versus-408 sentence, while leaving subgroup eligibility to a separate check. Current code returns None.

findings.title: REDUCE-IT bleeding refusal is audited as though no value exists

claim.quote:
"outcome": "Bleeding",
        "outcome_kind": "harm",
        "trial_key": "30415628",
        "label": "30415628",
        "id": "PMID 30415628",
        "stated_reason_code": "REFUSED_ON_EVIDENCE",
        "verdict": "REASON_WRONG_KIND",
        "detail": "value absent from held source, but the code names a value-present/refusal cause"

evidence.quote: Serious bleeding events occurred in 2.7% of the patients in the icosapent ethyl group and in 2.1% in the placebo group (P=0.06).

findings.why_wrong: The percentages are explicitly held. A decision not to reconstruct counts from rounded percentages can be valid, but the audit's explanation that the value is absent is false.
findings.served_effect: The audit incorrectly challenges an evidence-based refusal and conflates reported-but-not-pooled data with source absence.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input the held bleeding sentence to reason_audit.find_value_in_sources with the configured bleeding keywords. Assert numeric evidence is detected; then assert audit_reason_row does not explain REFUSED_ON_EVIDENCE as a missing value. Current numeric detection returns None.

findings.title: A post-hoc GISSI-HF report is assigned a primary-report role

evidence.quote: This post-hoc analysis of the GISSI-HF trial assessed the effect of n-3 PUFAs on AF in patients with chronic HF without AF at study entry over a median follow-up of 3.9 years.
Of these, 1140 (16.3%) had AF at baseline ECG and were excluded from the present analysis.

findings.why_wrong: The abstract explicitly identifies a post-hoc analysis restricted to participants without baseline AF. Its RCT publication type does not establish that this is the primary trial report.
findings.served_effect: The secondary report is included and represented with a primary role, creating misleading report identity and outcome-completeness accounting. This finding does not assert duplicate numerical pooling.
findings.proposed_fixture: Classify the held PMID 23839902 record, retaining both its RCT publication type and its post-hoc abstract language. Assert publication_role is secondary rather than primary and that it is linked to GISSI-HF rather than treated as an independent primary report.

findings.title: REDUCE-IT's triglyceride threshold is copied into the dose field

evidence.quote: a fasting triglyceride level of 135 to 499 mg per deciliter
The patients were randomly assigned to receive 2 g of icosapent ethyl twice daily (total daily dose, 4 g) or placebo.

findings.why_wrong: 499 mg is extracted from an eligibility concentration of 499 mg per deciliter. The intervention dose is explicitly 2 g twice daily, totaling 4 g daily.
findings.served_effect: REDUCE-IT carries incorrect dosing metadata in its intervention ontology and compatibility dimensions.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input the held PMID 30415628 abstract to intervention-ontology extraction. Assert dose represents 4 g/day or 2 g twice daily and never 499 mg; retain the triglyceride range only as population-enrichment information.

findings.title: REDUCE-IT's primary definition is attached to its secondary estimate

claim.quote: "endpoint_definition": "REDUCE-IT: 5-point primary (adds unstable angina, revascularization).; DISCLOSED (composite-heterogeneity note on the pool)"

evidence.quote: The key secondary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.
the corresponding rates of the key secondary end point were 11.2% and 14.8% (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.83; P<0.001).

findings.why_wrong: The selected REDUCE-IT result is HR 0.74 for the three-component secondary endpoint. Its endpoint_definition instead describes the five-component primary endpoint, apparently inherited from the older definition-audit entry.
findings.served_effect: The compatibility metadata describes a different endpoint from the pooled estimate and falsely attributes extra components to that selected result.
findings.proposed_fixture: Use the held REDUCE-IT secondary registry result and existing definition-audit row as inputs to compatibility derivation. Assert endpoint_definition follows the selected three-component result and cannot be overridden by the primary-endpoint audit description.

findings.title: ASCEND AF result inherits a vascular efficacy endpoint definition

claim.quote: "endpoint_definition": "primary outcome was a first serious vascular event (i"

evidence.quote:
"title": "Number of Participants With Event: Atrial Fibrillation (Omega-3 Comparison Only)",
        "description": "Includes fatal and non-fatal events."

findings.why_wrong: This endpoint_definition belongs to the served AF row for PMID 30146932. Its selected registry result measures AF, not the trial's primary serious-vascular-event composite.
findings.served_effect: The harm result carries an unrelated efficacy definition into compatibility metadata.
findings.proposed_fixture: Derive compatibility metadata for the held ASCEND AF registry outcome with its 166/7740 and 135/7740 counts. Assert the endpoint definition identifies AF and does not contain the primary serious-vascular-event definition.

findings.title: Comparator is called same-question despite broader interventions and controls

claim.quote: same-question comparator (matching intervention level and population)

evidence.quote: Bemelmans 2002  [ 27 ] Netherlands 266 (109/157) 54.1 44.0 NA 49.2 48.5 NA Primary a-linolenic acid vs omega-6 2.0 yr 4
(3) control (omega-6 fatty acid supplementation, placebo, or usual care)

findings.why_wrong: The topic is restricted to marine omega-3 in double-blind placebo/inert-control RCTs. The held comparator includes plant-derived alpha-linolenic acid and permits active omega-6 controls and usual care. A generic omega-3 class match does not establish the same question.
findings.served_effect: A broader synthesis is presented as scope-valid without identifying these intervention and comparator differences.
findings.proposed_fixture: Assess scope using the current topic configuration plus the held comparator inclusion criteria and Bemelmans table row. Assert an explicit intervention/comparator scope mismatch rather than an unconditional same-question verdict.

findings.title: Comparator's available MACE subset size is declared unavailable

claim.quote: The outcome-specific MACE subset is not separately machine-extractable from the cached text; 28 is the comparator meta size.

evidence.quote: Twenty-two RCTs showed the effect of omega-3 fatty acids on the risk of MACEs.

findings.why_wrong: The held full text directly states the outcome-specific count as 22. Although 28 is the overall review size, the claim that the MACE count is unavailable is contradicted by a simple held sentence.
findings.served_effect: The comparator overlap panel uses the overall 28-trial denominator while concealing the available 22-trial MACE denominator.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input the held sentence beginning 'Twenty-two RCTs' to comparator count extraction. Assert MACE-specific k equals 22, overall-review k remains separately 28, and the unavailable-subset claim is not emitted.

findings.title: Held comparator trial table is reported as not exposed

claim.quote: No comparator trial-list enumeration was found in the cached comparator text.

evidence.quote: Table 1 The summary characteristics in eligible study and involved individuals. Study Country Sample size Mean age (yr) Male (%) BMI (kg/m2) Smoking (%) Hypertension (%) DM (%) Prevention Intervention Follow-up Study quality

findings.why_wrong: The held full text contains a labeled trial-characteristics table with named study rows. The implementation returns measured absence when no topic-specific parsing profile exists; that is a parser-coverage limitation, not evidence that enumeration is absent.
findings.served_effect: The served comparator trial set is empty and labeled MEASURED_ABSENCE, preventing source-based overlap assessment.
